title: Harness Engineering for AI-Native Organizations: Four Behavioral Gates, Credential-Free MCP, and Continuous Drift Telemetry
author: Tech With RJ (synthesized by Brain Harness)

claims.assertion: Manual line-by-line code review is the primary bottleneck of AI-assisted engineering; sustainable velocity requires inverting trust from the AI model to the automated behavioral harness.
claims.source: Tech With RJ: 'How I Used Harness Engineering to Make Our Company AI-Native' (freeCodeCamp, Sept 2026)

claims.assertion: Agent code generation reliability is bounded by 4 behavioral gates (static typecheck, 100% core logic branch coverage, end-to-end user simulation, and live execution verification) rather than AST style linting.

Enterprise MCP servers must hold zero credentials and no direct database connections, forwarding user personal access tokens (PATs) to enforce live server-side RBAC and attribute audit trails to real human identities.
claims.source: Tech With RJ: MCP Security Model (2026) + Anthropic MCP Specification

claims.assertion: AI-native systems require tracking process drift and negative demand telemetry: unanswered agent questions form a prioritized documentation backlog, while CI code changes invalidate linked documentation sign-offs.
claims.source: Tech With RJ: Regulated Lending Documentation Platform Case Study (2026)
